# RSOS Language: exact shared state for AI agents

> The model names what should change; a deterministic runtime computes every value, checks every agent's copy against a state digest and repairs drift with zero model calls. The planner never sees a state value. Apache 2.0. Every prediction is published before its run; failures are kept.

Results (pre-registered, sealed):
- 318 of 320 tasks exact across six models from four companies, at 0.45-0.61x the cost per correct task; the 2 failures were refused by the runtime, none silent.
- A9, tasks drawn from a public randomness beacon after predictions were public: blind planning 48/48; Python that sees the state 48/48; blind Python 47/48; one-call JSON Patch 46/48 (all bad steps in the last quarter of the plan); tool-calling agent 15/16 at about 100 model calls per task.
- Error-window law: one-call JSON Patch per-step error rises from 0.19 % to 2.33 % across a plan (Mantel-Haenszel OR 12.3, 95 % CI 6.1-24.7); blind planning stays flat; the same pattern in a real SQLite engine.
- Not held: 26 of 76 agent predictions failed (all reported); blind planning was not more compact than plain Python.
